name: Agreement with the Pawnee, November 23, 1892, ratified March 3, 1893
aka: Pawnee allotment and cession agreement of 1892
citation: Act of March 3, 1893, ch. 209, sec. 12, 27 Stat. 612, 644
promises: The Pawnee ceded their reservation between the Cimarron and Arkansas rivers subject to allotments in severalty to tribal members (27 Stat. 644; ICC Docket 10).

The United States agreed to pay $1.25 an acre for all surplus land after allotment: $80,000 per capita on ratification and the rest credited to the tribe in the Treasury at 5 percent interest (27 Stat. 644; ICC Docket 10, finding 160).

breaches.what: On a Senate reference, the Court of Claims found that of the 170,333.37 acres of surplus land the United States disposed of under the 1892 agreement, the tribe was owed $212,916.71 at $1.25 an acre; after the $80,000 paid, neither the $132,916.71 balance nor any interest on it from March 3, 1893 had been paid. It reported a just claim, its payment resting with Congress.
breaches.whoFoundIt: Pawnee Tribe of Indians v. United States, 56 Ct. Cl. 1 (1920), finding VII and conclusions

breaches.quote: Neither this principal sum of $132,916.71 nor any interest thereon has been paid.

breaches.what: The Indian Claims Commission held that surplus land ceded under the 1892 agreement had to be paid for under its terms. For 88.43 acres patented to the town of Pawnee in 1907, the $110.55 was credited only around March 17, 1921 and the agreed 5 percent interest from 1893 was never paid; for 25.54 acres patented to the Southern Baptist Home Mission Board in 1920 the tribe received no payment. It awarded $155.00 and $31.90 with interest (Claims VI and VII).

landTaken: The Court of Claims, as summarized by the Commission, found 171,088.37 acres of surplus land after allotment, of which 755 acres were reserved for school and agency use (ICC Docket 10, finding 160).
compensation: Under the agreement $1.25 an acre was due on the surplus. In 1920 the Court of Claims (56 Ct. Cl. 1) found the $132,916.71 balance for 170,333.37 acres, and the 5 percent interest from March 3, 1893, still unpaid. The Docket 10 final award of July 6, 1962 included $155.00 for Claim VI and $31.90 with interest for Claim VII.
today: Not researched past the 1962 final award.

openQuestions: The breaches the Commission found are small: unpaid interest and an unpaid 25.54 acres. No ruling on whether $1.25 an acre was itself unconscionable was found for this cession.
Claim V in Docket 10 concerns a 4,800-acre strip of the Nebraska reservation paid for in 1875; it belongs to the earlier Nebraska cessions, not this record.
The Pawnee Nation website returned 403 to an automated request; its account was not read.

Audit 2026-11-08 (round 14): added the 1920 Court of Claims finding. The researcher could not find the report under '54 Ct. Cl. 1', the citation in the ICC's damaged scan; it is reported at 56 Ct. Cl. 1 (Caselaw Access Project, findings in the head matter). The court's interest totals differ between its finding ($182,760.32) and its conclusion ($182,860.32), so no interest figure is recorded. When and whether Congress paid the $132,916.71 was not traced; the ICC's note that the 88.43-acre payment was credited about March 17, 1921 suggests a 1921 settlement but does not say so.

plain.promised: In 1892 the Pawnee gave up their Oklahoma reservation except for individual allotments. The United States promised $1.25 an acre for the rest, with interest on what it held.
plain.happened: In 1920 the Court of Claims found the United States had still not paid most of the agreed price, $132,916.71, or any interest since 1893. The Indian Claims Commission later found more land paid for late or never.
plain.today: The Commission awarded $155.00 and $31.90 with interest, part of a larger 1962 award.
